subject: US Economics Analyst: Productivity Stagnation in the Construction Industry: An International Perspective
summary: Labor productivity is real output per hour worked, and its measurement in construction hinges on the output price index used to deflate nominal output. Structures are highly heterogeneous, so isolating pure price change from quality change is difficult. Two methods exist: a top-down approach that tracks sale prices of new units against observed characteristics, and a bottom-up approach that aggregates input costs plus a profit margin. subject: US Economics Analyst: Higher Oil Prices and the Risk of Fed Hikes
summary: Since the start of the Iran war, oil prices have risen and markets have repriced the Fed sharply toward hikes. This note argues the FOMC is unlikely to hike and lays out four reasons: the shock is smaller and narrower than prior inflationary episodes; the economy's starting point (loose labor market, sub-target wage growth, anchored expectations) limits second-round effects; policy already sits near neutral and financial conditions have tightened ~80bp; and the Fed historically does not tighten on oil shocks alone.
